title: Portrait camera hides most of the players and wastes the top ~45% of the screen
evidence: Measured with Playwright (390x844, seed 7, after damping converged): with the ball handler on the right wing (5.4,-7.6) the camera sits at (4.03, 11, 8) fov 70 and the NDC x of the other players are: left-wing teammate feet -1.53, left-corner teammate -1.41, two defenders -1.29/-1.25 -> 4 of 6 players are off-screen, rim at x=-0.57 (screenshot test/scratch/shots/phonePortrait-wing.png shows only 2 players). In the CHECK formation the court spans NDC y 0.106 (far baseline) .. -0.621 (half-court line) = 36% of the screen height, the banner top is at y 0.517 so 24% of the screen is pure black above the arena and ~21% is crowd/banner; the near end of the court is 1.9x the viewport width (near corners at x=-1.83/+1.95). PORTRAIT = { fov: 70, kx: 0.80, y: 11.0, z0: 8.0 } (spec section 9 numbers) produces this.
failure: On a phone held upright the user cannot see the teammates they are passing to or the defenders on the weak side whenever the ball is on a wing, and the hoop slides to the screen edge; the playable court is a 36%-tall band in the middle of the screen while the top quarter is empty background.
proposedFix: Change the portrait framing (spec section 9 values need updating with it): reduce kx to ~0.35 so the far side stays in view, lower the camera (y ~9.5, z0 ~7) and tilt the look point nearer (lookZ ~-8, lookY ~1.5) so the far baseline lands around NDC y 0.5 and the half-court line near -0.8; keep the paint zoom and verify A21 (rim + ball in [-1,1]) and A20/A26 still pass. Alternatively use a wider horizontal fov by setting fov from the horizontal angle (fov = 2*atan(tan(hfov/2)/aspect)) so aspect 0.46 keeps the whole 15.2 m width.
adjustedFixes: Minimal, spec-consistent tweak (update SPEC.md section 9 portrait line together with it): in src/camera.js change only PORTRAIT.lookZ from -9.0 to -7.0 (optionally -6.0). Offline projection with the vendored three.js (same maths as camera.js) at aspect 390/844: lookZ -7 moves the CHECK court band from NDC y 0.11..-0.62 to 0.19..-0.53 (lookZ -6: 0.23..-0.48) and the backboard top from 0.32 to 0.41, reclaiming roughly 8-12% of the screen height from the empty top band; A21 worst |ndc| stays 0.87 (rim + ball in view for every clamped ball position), kx/fov/y/z0 unchanged so A20/A26 and the paint zoom are unaffected. If the weak side should also be less cut off, the best framing that still passes A21 is PORTRAIT = { fov: 74, kx: 0.65, y: 12.5, z0: 9.5, lookY: 1.0, lookZ: -7.0 } (A21 worst 0.60, wing-handler rim x -0.43 instead of -0.61, left defender x -0.87 on-screen instead of -1.15, weak-side wing -1.21 instead of -1.58, court band 0.17..-0.43, handler ~45 px tall instead of 57); it cannot bring the opposite wing fully on-screen, so do not adopt the finding's kx 0.35 or the horizontal-fov formula. Keep the existing #rotateHint as the answer for full-width visibility. Verify with node test/acceptance.cjs A20 A21 A26.

In src/camera.js line 12 change PORTRAIT to { fov: 74, kx: 0.40, y: 13.0, z0: 10.0, kz: 0, lookY: 0.0, lookZ: -6.0 } (higher, further back, slightly wider, looking nearer, panning less with the ball). Verified by projection at aspect 390/844: with the ball at (5.4,-7.6) the left wing / left corner / weak-side defenders land at x -0.99 / -0.95 / -0.77 / -0.81 (all on screen, rim at about -0.3); over all clamped ball extremes ((+-7.62, 0), (+-7.62,-14.3), etc.) rim and ball stay within |NDC| <= 0.87 so A21 keeps passing; the court band becomes y 0.26..-0.31 with the backboard top at 0.42 (centred instead of sunk to the lower half), and viewport coverage of the offensive half rises from 62% to 85%. If fov must stay 70, the best alternative is { fov: 70, kx: 0.45, y: 12, z0: 10, lookY: 0, lookZ: -6 } (coverage 78%, wing players at -1.14/-1.08/-0.89/-0.93, so the far corner is still marginal). Keep kz = 0 and the paint zoom of -4 unchanged; re-run 'node test/acceptance.cjs A20 A21 A26' and the camera unit test. Do not adopt the finding's kx 0.35 / y 9.5 / z0 7 / lookZ -8 values (ball at the near sideline goes off-screen at x=1.50).

title: Adaptive DPR downgrade keys on the rAF interval, so a throttled display (30 Hz / low-power mode) permanently halves resolution
evidence: perfMon.frame(frameDt * 1000) records the requestAnimationFrame interval (frameDt = min((now-last)/1000, 0.1)), not the time spent in game.render + renderer.render. shouldDowngrade() (scene.js:313) is sticky: after 5 s of frames averaging > 24 ms it calls renderer.setPixelRatio(1.0) once for the session (main.js:249-255). The loop also runs (and is measured) while the main menu is open before the game starts.
failure: On an iPhone in Low Power Mode (Safari caps rAF at 30 fps -> 33 ms frames), on 30 Hz external displays, or when the artifact iframe is throttled/occluded, the game drops from DPR 1.5 to 1.0 after 5 s even though the GPU is idle, and the softer image never comes back for the session. The downgrade frame also renders twice (resize() at main.js:253 renders, then renderFrame renders again).
proposedFix: Feed the monitor the measured busy time of the frame (performance.now() around game.render + renderer.render + hud.update) instead of the rAF interval, or ignore samples where busy time < 60% of the interval; start the monitor only once state is LIVE (reset it in game 'start'); skip the extra render in resize() when called from the downgrade path.
adjustedFixes: Keep the rAF-interval signal (it is the only JS-visible symptom of a GPU-bound device) but stop it misfiring on throttled displays, and fix the two side issues: (1) In main.js, before startLoop() at boot, sample ~20 requestAnimationFrame intervals with no rendering (median = the display/rAF cadence, e.g. 16.7 ms on 60 Hz, 33 ms on 30 Hz or iOS Low Power Mode) and construct PerfMonitor with thresholdMs = Math.max(PERF.DOWNGRADE_MS, 1.4 * cadenceMs); a 60 Hz display keeps the spec's 24 ms threshold while a 30 Hz display needs > 46 ms average frames (a real slowdown) to downgrade. (2) Start counting only once the game is LIVE: recreate/reset the PerfMonitor in hud.cb.onStart (or on game 'start'), so menu time never contributes to the 5 s warm-up (consistent with SPEC A25 measuring performance 'after 5 s of LIVE'). (3) Avoid the double render on the downgrade frame: give resize() a parameter (e.g. resize(skipRender)) and call resize(true) from the downgrade path since renderFrame renders immediately afterwards. No change to PerfMonitor or constants; the sticky-for-session behaviour required by the spec stays.

title: Shot meter is projected with the previous frame's camera matrixWorldInverse
evidence: game.render() (game.js:1167-1183) runs cam.update() then renderMeter() -> hud.projectMeter() -> SCRATCH.v3a.set(x,y,z).project(cam). Vector3.project uses camera.matrixWorldInverse, which three.js only refreshes inside renderer.render() (called afterwards in main.js renderFrame, line 224). camera.apply() (camera.js:94-104) only sets position/rotation and updates the projection matrix.
failure: While the camera is still panning/zooming during a windup or layup (ball entering the paint triggers the fov damp and the x follow), the meter is drawn against the shooter's head position of one frame ago, so it visibly trails the head by a few px each frame instead of sticking to it.
proposedFix: In BroadcastCamera.apply() after setting position/rotation call c.updateMatrixWorld(true); c.matrixWorldInverse.copy(c.matrixWorld).invert(); (or do that in projectMeter before .project). Cost is one 4x4 inverse per frame.

title: Ball allocates its own blob texture and shadow plane instead of sharing the humanoid ones
evidence: ball.js:62-64: new THREE.PlaneGeometry(0.9,0.9).rotateX(...) and blob = makeBlobTexture() (a second 64x64 canvas + GPU texture) although humanoid.js:81/94 already builds the identical shared shadow geometry and blob texture (spec section 6: 'Ball shadow same texture scaled 0.35'). Measured renderer.info.memory: textures 6 (court, ball, board, banner, blob x2), geometries 21. Budget numbers otherwise fine: 91 draw calls (menu 88), 9212 triangles, 64 line segments, 11 programs; scene.children 21 and info.memory unchanged after 5 rematch() and 5 quit()/start() cycles; heap sampling shows ~0 allocations in game.step/game.render/hud.update/input.sample (three's own renderer.render ~660 B/frame).
failure: One redundant 64x64 texture upload and one extra geometry per boot; no visible effect, but violates the shared-asset rule and duplicates the shadow look-alike if either is tuned later.
proposedFix: Export the shared shadow geometry/material from humanoid.js (buildSharedGeometry().shadow and getSharedMaterials().blob) and reuse them in Ball, creating only the per-ball MeshBasicMaterial (opacity is animated) with map: sharedBlob.
adjustedFixes: In src/humanoid.js export the material accessor (change `function getSharedMaterials()` at line 89 to `export function getSharedMaterials()`), or add a tiny `export function getSharedShadowAssets() { return { geometry: buildSharedGeometry().shadow, blob: getSharedMaterials().blob }; }`. In src/ball.js replace lines 62-64: drop the `makeBlobTexture` import (keep makeBallTexture), import `{ buildSharedGeometry, getSharedMaterials }` from './humanoid.js', and use `const shadowGeo = buildSharedGeometry().shadow; const blob = getSharedMaterials().blob;` (getSharedMaterials already wraps makeBlobTexture in try/catch and yields blob=null in headless node, so the existing `color: blob ? 0xffffff : 0x000000` fallback still works). Keep the per-ball MeshBasicMaterial since its opacity is animated (0.5 -> 0.15 with height), unlike the shared humanoid material at opacity 0.45. Do not add any dispose() of the shadow geometry/texture in Ball (nothing disposes today, and they are now shared). Expected result: renderer.info.memory.textures drops from 6 to 5 and geometries by 1; run `node test/unit-ball.mjs`, `node test/unit-humanoid.mjs` and `node test/acceptance.cjs` to confirm nothing regresses.

In src/humanoid.js, export getSharedMaterials (change `function getSharedMaterials()` to `export function getSharedMaterials()`; buildSharedGeometry is already exported). In src/ball.js, replace the import of makeBlobTexture with `import { buildSharedGeometry, getSharedMaterials } from './humanoid.js';` (keep makeBallTexture from scene.js), and replace lines 62-64 with: `const shadowGeo = buildSharedGeometry().shadow; const blob = getSharedMaterials().blob;` (getSharedMaterials already wraps makeBlobTexture in try/catch and yields blob=null headlessly, so the existing `color: blob ? 0xffffff : 0x000000` fallback still works). Keep the per-ball `this.shadowMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ map: blob, ... })` since its opacity is animated in update(). Optionally add an assertion in test/unit-humanoid.mjs or a new ball unit test that `ball.shadow.geometry === buildSharedGeometry().shadow` and `ball.shadowMat.map === getSharedMaterials().blob`, and update the acceptance/perf expectation from 6 textures to 5.

title: Backboard is a DoubleSide transparent box with depthWrite off, so its faces stack and it reads ~0.6 opaque instead of 0.35
evidence: court.js:199-204: BoxGeometry (6 faces) with MeshLambertMaterial { transparent, opacity 0.35, depthWrite: false, side: THREE.DoubleSide }. From the court-side camera the front face, the back face (visible through the front because nothing writes depth) and the 4 edge faces are all blended: 1 - 0.65^2 = 0.58 effective opacity, and the 256^2 target-square texture is also stretched onto the 4 thin edge faces. Visible in test/shots/integ-desktop-live.png as a milky grey slab rather than a glass board.

The camera is always on the +z side of the board, so no visible face is lost.

Minimal, spec-consistent fix in /home/user/aqualink-app/games/nba2k-threejs/src/court.js line 202: change `side: THREE.DoubleSide` to `side: THREE.FrontSide` (or simply delete the `side:` entry, since FrontSide is the default). title: Rotate hint stays on screen during play, covering the play-by-play caption and intercepting touches
evidence: showMenu() (lines 399-410) only toggles PANELS/OVERLAYS and #menus; #rotateHint is never hidden when the game starts (game.start -> hud.showMenu(null)). CSS: #rotateHint { z-index:12; top:calc(80px + safe-top); pointer-events:auto } (lines 447-465) vs #caption { top:calc(84px + safe-top) } inside #hud (z-index 1). Measured in 390x844 after tapping Start without dismissing (test/scratch/misc2.cjs): state LIVE, hintVisible true, hint box [96,80,198,48], caption text box [112,85,166,21], overlap true, document.elementFromPoint at the hint centre returns the hint, not the HUD. Screenshot test/scratch/shots/portrait-live-hint.png: the '横屏体验更佳 / 知道了' pill sits over the caption slot on top of the court during LIVE play.
failure: A first-time portrait player who taps 开始比赛 without tapping 知道了 (the natural flow: the big orange Start button is the obvious target) plays the whole game with the hint pill floating over the court exactly where captions (三分命中, 抢断, 违例…) render; the captions are hidden behind it for the entire session and the pill eats taps in that area.

Alternatively give #rotateHint an auto-timeout (e.g. 6 s) and place it below the caption band. Also consider showing it only while #menuMain is visible (`#menus.hidden ~ #rotateHint{display:none}`).

E.g. after `this.menu = name || null;` add: `if (!name && e.rotateHint) e.rotateHint.classList.add('hidden');`. (If you prefer treating Start as acknowledgement, call `this.dismissRotateHint()` there instead, which also sets the localStorage flag.) Minimal, in /home/user/aqualink-app/games/nba2k-threejs/src/hud.js showMenu(): when gameplay starts or resumes (name is null/falsy) hide the pill without persisting the localStorage flag, so A22 semantics (persist only on explicit 知道了; hint reappears at the main menu on the next launch until acknowledged) are unchanged. After the PANELS/OVERLAYS toggles add: `if (!name && e.rotateHint) e.rotateHint.classList.add('hidden');`. Do not call dismissRotateHint() there (it would set hoop.rotateHintSeen without the user acknowledging). The existing resize handler and btnRotateDismiss stay as they are. title: Joystick starts moving the player immediately when the thumb lands within 24 px of a screen edge (clamp shifts the ring centre but the vector is computed from the original touch point)
evidence: _onStickDown clamps s.cx/s.cy to >= 24 px from the viewport edge (lines 191-197) and then immediately calls _updateStickVector(e.clientX, e.clientY) (line 203) with the unclamped finger position, so the first sample already carries a deflection. Measured on 844x390 LIVE via CDP touch with no touchMove (test/scratch/absence.cjs): touchStart at x=4 -> stick cx=24, intent.move = {x:-0.24, z:0, mag:0.24}; touchStart at y=386 -> intent.move.z = +0.24 (player walks backward toward the baseline).
failure: In landscape the joystick zone reaches the bottom edge, and thumbs routinely land in the bottom 24 px; the controlled player drifts sideways/backward at ~24 % speed without any thumb movement, which reads as input lag or 'the player moves on his own', and can push the ball handler out of bounds near the sideline.
proposedFix: Keep the clamp for the drawn ring but make the initial vector zero: after clamping, set s.vx=s.vz=s.mag=0, s.knobX=e.clientX-s.cx, s.knobY=e.clientY-s.cy and only call _updateStickVector from pointermove; or offset the vector origin by the clamp delta (store s.ox=e.clientX-s.cx, s.oy=e.clientY-s.cy and subtract it in _updateStickVector until the finger has moved more than the dead zone).
adjustedFixes: Minimal change in src/input.js _onStickDown: keep the clamp for the ring position, but do not derive the initial vector from the unclamped touch point. Replace line 203 `this._updateStickVector(e.clientX, e.clientY);` with nothing (the vector/knob were already zeroed on line 200), so the first non-zero sample only comes from pointermove via the existing _onStickMove -> _updateStickVector path. Because subsequent pointermove samples still measure from the clamped centre, a finger that lands at x=4 and then moves 1 px will jump to ~0.24 deflection; if that step is considered unacceptable, additionally record the clamp offset in _onStickDown (`s.ox = e.clientX - s.cx; s.oy = e.clientY - s.cy;`) and in _updateStickVector use `dx = (px - s.ox) - s.cx, dy = (py - s.oy) - s.cy`, decaying s.ox/s.oy to 0 once the finger has left the dead zone (or simply keeping the offset for the life of that touch, which makes the ring a purely visual clamp and the vector origin the real touch point, consistent with §3.2 "ring appears at the touch point"). Reset s.ox = s.oy = 0 in _releaseStick. title: Sticky DPR downgrade is judged from frames rendered under the menu/pause backdrop-filter blur, not from gameplay frames

The downgrade is sticky (downgraded=true, PerfMonitor.downgraded) and can therefore be triggered by a 2 s window spent in the main menu or pause menu, where the fullscreen blur of a live canvas is the most expensive frame the page ever produces on mid-range Android GPUs; the decision is never revisited when the blur goes away.

Optionally, when a menu closes (hud.menu transitions from non-null to null), discard the stale window by constructing a fresh PerfMonitor or adding a small `reset()` to PerfMonitor (scene.js) that zeroes head/count/sum but keeps elapsedMs, so the 2 s window is not contaminated by the last blurred frames. Do not change PERF constants, the sticky semantics, or the unit test in test/unit-court.mjs:181 (it exercises PerfMonitor directly and stays valid). Replacing the backdrop blur or freezing renderer.render under menus is not needed for the fix and would touch spec-described rendering behaviour, so leave it out.

adjustedFixes: Minimal, spec-consistent fix: in src/hud.js add `clearCaptions() { this._queue.length = 0; this._capT = -1; this._capFading = false; this._capCur = null; const el = this.els.caption; if (el) { el.classList.remove('show'); this._text(el, ''); } }` and call `if (this.hud) this.hud.clearCaptions();` from Game.start() (next to `this.hud.showMenu(null)`, src/game.js:228; rematch() goes through start() so it is covered) and from Game.quit() (next to `this.banner(null)`, src/game.js:248). Do NOT clear in gameOver(): the spec (§1 quarter buzzer, §8 'buzzer-beater caption on make') requires the final make/`cap.buzzerBeater` caption to be shown, and it is queued immediately before gameOver() runs, so clearing there would suppress it. Likewise do not clear at every enterCheck, which would drop legitimate end-of-period captions queued just before QUARTER_END. Optionally add an acceptance check: after GAME_OVER + rematch(), `__game.hud._queue.length === 0` and `#caption` lacks class 'show'; after quit(), same assertion with #menuMain visible.

title: Language toggle does not re-render the banner currently on screen
evidence: refreshLang() (lines 215-230) re-labels team buttons, lang button, period (`_lastQ = -1`), the game-over and halftime panels and the current caption, but the banner text set by banner() is never re-rendered. Scenario lang: with the CHECK banner up, hud.toggleLanguage() → period 'Q1', buttons BLOCK/SWITCH/STEAL, caption 'Shi Yue scores', pause panel English, but `#banner` still '发球' (expected 'CHECK BALL'); same for quarter-end/overtime/final banners (up to 2.5 s).
failure: Right after toggling language (T key or pause menu) the large centred banner stays in the previous language while everything else switches; spec §11 says all HUD text goes through t() and the toggle relabels everything.
proposedFix: Store `_bannerKey/_bannerParams` in banner() and, in refreshLang(), `if (this._bannerT > 0 && this._bannerKey) this._text(this.els.banner, t(this._bannerKey, localizeParams(this._bannerParams)))`; do the same for the meter flash text if desired.
adjustedFixes: In src/hud.js: (1) in the constructor next to `this._bannerT = 0;` add `this._bannerKey = null; this._bannerParams = null;`. (2) In banner(): on the `!key` early-return also clear `this._bannerKey = null;`; otherwise store `this._bannerKey = key; this._bannerParams = params || null;` before `this._text(el, t(key, localizeParams(params)))`. (3) In _tickBanner(), when the banner expires (`_bannerT <= 0`) also set `this._bannerKey = null`. (4) At the end of refreshLang() add: `if (this._bannerT > 0 && this._bannerKey) this._text(this.els.banner, t(this._bannerKey, localizeParams(this._bannerParams)));`. This mirrors the existing `_capCur` handling for captions, keeps all text through t()/localizeParams, and needs no change to game.js or the spec. The meter flash (0.6 s) can be left as is.

In src/hud.js: in banner(), after the early-return for !key, store `this._bannerKey = key; this._bannerParams = params || null;` (and clear both in the !key branch). In refreshLang(), add `if (this._bannerT > 0 && this._bannerKey) this._text(this.els.banner, t(this._bannerKey, localizeParams(this._bannerParams)));`. title: P/Escape (and M/T) during HALFTIME both skip the halftime and pause/mute/toggle, because the HUD 'any key skips' handler does not exclude the Input hotkeys
evidence: hud.js line 136 registers a document keydown that calls onSkip for any key while menu === 'halftime'; input.js line 363 registers its own document keydown that calls _pause() for KeyP/Escape regardless of `enabled`. Both fire (HUD first). Scenario halftimeKey (real page.keyboard.press('KeyP') in HALFTIME): before {state HALFTIME, paused false} → after {state CHECK, quarter 3, paused true, #halftime hidden, #menuPause visible}.
failure: A desktop player pressing P/Esc to pause at halftime instead skips the halftime overlay, starts Q3's CHECK and lands in the pause menu; M/T similarly skip the halftime as a side effect.
proposedFix: In the HUD halftime keydown handler ignore the reserved codes: `if (['KeyP','Escape','KeyM','KeyT'].includes(ev.code)) return;` (or have Input.onPause consult hud.menu === 'halftime' and no-op), so those keys keep their single meaning.

title: Pausing during QUARTER_END/CHECK discards the period banner; after the resume countdown nothing restores it
evidence: pause() calls `this.banner(null)` (line 260) and stepPaused() shows the countdown then `this.banner(null)` (line 580); the QUARTER_END/CHECK banner key is not remembered. Scenario pause.quarterEndPause: banner '第3节结束' shown → game.pause() → game.resume() + 1.1 s → `#banner` text '1', show class removed, state still QUARTER_END for its remaining time.
failure: Pausing right at a quarter buzzer (or when the tab is hidden, which auto-pauses) loses the 'END OF Q3'/'OVERTIME'/'FINAL'/'CHECK BALL' banner; on resume the player sees a silent quarter break with no indication of what happened.
proposedFix: In pause(), stash the HUD's current banner key/params and remaining ms (expose them from HUD.banner) and re-issue `this.banner(key, params, remainingMs)` at the end of stepPaused() when the countdown finishes, instead of banner(null).
adjustedFixes: Minimal, spec-consistent: (1) hud.js: in banner(key, params, ms) remember `this._bannerKey = key; this._bannerParams = params || null;` (clear them in the `!key` branch) and add `bannerState() { return this._bannerT > 0 && this._bannerKey ? { key: this._bannerKey, params: this._bannerParams, ms: Math.ceil(this._bannerT * 1000) } : null; }`. (2) game.js pause(): before `this.banner(null)` do `this.pausedBanner = this.hud ? this.hud.bannerState() : null;`. (3) game.js stepPaused(): replace the final `this.banner(null);` with `const b = this.pausedBanner; this.pausedBanner = null; if (b) this.banner(b.key, b.params, b.ms); else this.banner(null);`. (4) Reset `this.pausedBanner = null` in start(), quit() and gameOver() so a stale banner cannot leak across games/menus. This restores END OF Qn / OVERTIME / FINAL / CHECK BALL (and +2/+3) for their remaining duration after the countdown, without touching the state machine or clocks. Add a test: pause during QUARTER_END, resume, fastForward 1.1 s, assert #banner has .show and text matches banner.quarterEnd while state is still QUARTER_END.

title: STL is credited (and 'steals it!' captioned) on the poke, even when the offence recovers the ball and keeps possession
evidence: trySteal() increments `p.stats.stl` and emits cap.steal (lines 936-938) at the moment the ball is knocked loose; onCatch() then gives the loose ball back to the offence with `ctx === 'steal'` and no correction. Scenario stealRecover (human steal from 0.5 m, defenders then teleported away): stl after poke 1, offence (team 1 = w.offense) recovered the ball, shot clock untouched at 13.2, possession unchanged, final stl still 1 and caption '石岳 抢断！' displayed. Spec §1: 'a steal/interception counts as STL for the catcher'.
failure: Box score shows steals for possessions that never changed hands and the play-by-play announces a steal that did not happen; a defender can farm STL by repeatedly poking the ball loose.
proposedFix: Move the stat/caption to the outcome: in trySteal() only knock the ball loose (remember `this.stealBy = p`), and in onCatch() credit `stl++` + cap.steal when a defender (any defender, or the stealer) catches a `ctx === 'steal'` ball; do nothing when the offence recovers.
adjustedFixes: In src/game.js trySteal() remove the three lines `p.stats.stl++; this.caption('cap.steal', p); this.emit('steal', h, p);` (keep ball.launch, ballCtx='steal', stealVictim=h, shot.pending=false, return true). In onCatch() change the defensive branch to `if (prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal') { p.stats.stl++; this.caption('cap.steal', p); this.emit('steal', prev === 'pass' ? ball.passInfo.from : this.stealVictim, p); } else { p.stats.reb++; this.caption('cap.rebound', p); this.emit('rebound', 'defensive', p); }` and make the turnover reason `(prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal') ? 'STEAL' : 'REBOUND'`. The offensive-recovery path needs no change (it already resets ballCtx to 'none' without crediting). This credits STL to the catcher as spec §1 line 55 states, keeps A16 (cap.steal coincides with the possession change) and A15 (pass interception path unchanged) passing.

src/game.js only. (1) trySteal(): keep launching the ball loose, setting ballCtx='steal', stealVictim=h and shot.pending=false, but delete `p.stats.stl++`, `this.caption('cap.steal', p)` and `this.emit('steal', h, p)` (optionally emit a distinct 'poke' event if anyone wants the deflection itself; nothing in src listens today). (2) onCatch(), defensive branch: replace `if (prev === 'pass') { stl++; caption; emit('steal', passInfo.from, p) } else if (ctx !== 'steal') { reb... }` with `if (prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal') { p.stats.stl++; this.caption('cap.steal', p); this.emit('steal', prev === 'pass' ? ball.passInfo.from : this.stealVictim, p); } else { p.stats.reb++; this.caption('cap.rebound', p); this.emit('rebound', 'defensive', p); }` and use the same condition for the turnover reason: `this.emit('turnover', (prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal') ? 'STEAL' : 'REBOUND', p)`. The offence branch stays as is (no stat, ballCtx reset), so an offensive recovery of a poked ball credits nothing. Crediting the catcher (any defender) rather than remembering the poker matches SPEC line 55 ('STL for the catcher') and needs no new state; clear stealVictim wherever ballCtx is reset to 'none' if you want tidiness. A poked ball that goes out of bounds keeps the current OOB path and credits no STL.

In src/game.js trySteal() (lines 929-940) keep the launch, `this.ballCtx = 'steal'`, `this.stealVictim = h`, `this.shot.pending = false` and `return true`, but delete `p.stats.stl++`, `this.caption('cap.steal', p)` and `this.emit('steal', h, p)`. In onCatch() change the defensive branch to credit the catcher: `if (prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal') { p.stats.stl++; this.caption('cap.steal', p); this.emit('steal', ctx === 'steal' ? this.stealVictim : ball.passInfo.from, p); } else { p.stats.reb++; ...rebound... }` and pass `'STEAL'` to emit('turnover') when `prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'steal'`. The offence branch (line 1012) stays as is: an offensive recovery of a poked ball credits nothing and keeps the possession/shot clock, and an OOB/rest after a poke credits nothing either. Optionally clear `this.stealVictim = null` where ballCtx is reset. Update the stat comment at lines 1005-1006 accordingly; run `node test/acceptance.cjs A15 A16` and test/unit-ai.mjs (its mock already credits STL at the catch, line 126).

title: A pass that touches the floor and is then caught by the defence is booked as a defensive REB instead of a STL
evidence: onCatch() decides STL only from `prev === 'pass'` (line 1026); once Ball.step flips a floor-bounced pass to 'loose', the defensive catch falls into the `else if (ctx !== 'steal')` branch (line 1030) → reb++ and cap.rebound even though `this.ballCtx` is still 'pass'. Scenario passLoose: pass thrown onto the floor (ball state 'loose', ballCtx 'pass'), defender walked onto it → DEAD(TURNOVER), caption cap.rebound, events ['rebound','defensive',…], defender stats reb 1 stl 0.
failure: Interceptions of bad passes that bounce first show up as rebounds in the box score and play-by-play, while spec §1 counts an interception as STL for the catcher.
proposedFix: Use the ball context rather than the raw state: `if (prev === 'pass' || ctx === 'pass') { stl++; cap.steal } else if (ctx !== 'steal') { reb++ }` in onCatch().

title: CPU handler shoots the instant it catches (median 0.08 s) and almost always on the move
evidence: Auto game, normal, seed 7 (test/scratch/misc-probe.cjs): catch-to-shot-press delay for CPU handlers: 27 of 28 shots pressed < 0.2 s after the catch, median 0.08 s. Per-shot records from 3 auto games: shots released with shooter speed > 2.5 m/s (move penalty x0.85 applies) = 57/61 normal, 32/52 easy, 31/47 hard; release time since LIVE: normal 56/61 within 1.5-4 s (0.8 s setup + one pass + shot). Possession trace: 't1.2 Hu probe pos(4.1,-7.0) spd3.7 -> t1.4 Hu shoot* windup spd3.7'. Cause: handler() decides on the first 0.1 s tick after hadBall (lines 452-456, 480-512); SHOOT scores 0.5+0.2 = 0.7 > PROBE 0.4 as soon as open >= shootOpen, and the set-feet wait on line 533 only fires when defD > SHOOT_SET_CLEAR (2.2 m), which a guarded receiver never satisfies.
failure: CPU offence is a catch-and-shoot machine: pass to the wing, wing fires a running 6.5-7.5 m jumper 1-2 frames after the catch. No dribble, no reading the defence, the meter/windup is never visible on a stationary shooter, and the human on defence never gets a closeout opportunity.
proposedFix: Add a minimum hold after a catch before SHOOT is eligible (e.g. 0.3-0.5 s, like PASS_HOLD_MIN), make the set-feet brake apply whenever p.speed > MOVE_SPEED unless a defender is within ~1.0 m, and subtract the move penalty (x0.85) from the SHOOT utility so a running jumper scores below PROBE.
adjustedFixes: In src/ai.js, two small gates, no change to the spec §7.1 SHOOT score formula: (1) add `const SHOOT_HOLD_MIN = 0.35;` and in the utility block make SHOOT eligible only when `t - ai.holdSince >= SHOOT_HOLD_MIN` (same pattern as PASS_HOLD_MIN on line 501; `urgent` still forces SHOOT and the drive branch's startShot at DRIVE_FINISH_D is unaffected). (2) On line 533 lower the brake's defender threshold so it applies whenever the shooter is moving unless a defender can contest: replace `SHOOT_SET_CLEAR = 2.2` with ~1.0 (e.g. `SHOOT_SET_CONTEST = 1.0`), keeping the existing 0.35 s cap (`t - ai.actionT < SHOOT_SET_T`) so the shooter never waits longer than that. Re-run the probe to confirm the median catch-to-press delay rises to >= 0.35 s and most jumpers are released below 2.5 m/s; leave the score formula as specified.

Two small changes in src/ai.js, keeping the spec 7.1 SHOOT score formula untouched (do not fold the x0.85 move penalty into the utility; that would deviate from the spec's formula). (1) Add `const SHOOT_HOLD_MIN = 0.3;` next to PASS_HOLD_MIN and, in the handler utility block, gate SHOOT eligibility on hold time: compute the SHOOT score as now, then `if (s > bestScore && (t - ai.holdSince >= SHOOT_HOLD_MIN || d <= SHOT.LAYUP_D)) { best = 'shoot'; bestScore = s; }`. The urgent (shotClock < URGENT_CLOCK) path and the isUsersTeammate path are above this block and stay unchanged, so panic shots and the human's-teammate rules are unaffected; with HYSTERESIS 0.4 s the receiver probes for one cycle and the earliest catch-and-shoot lands ~0.4-0.5 s after the catch. (2) Make the set-feet brake fire whenever the shooter is moving unless a defender can reach the release: replace SHOOT_SET_CLEAR = 2.2 with a close-threat radius, e.g. `SHOOT_SET_THREAT = 1.0` (inside CONTEST_R 1.6 and where the 0.35 s BLOCK_WINDOW matters), and change line 533 to `if (p.speed > SHOT.MOVE_SPEED && t - ai.actionT < SHOOT_SET_T && d > SHOT.LAYUP_D && defD > SHOOT_SET_THREAT) break;`. stopMove(it) is already called before the switch, so the `break` path decelerates at MOVE.DECEL 16 m/s^2 and a 4 m/s receiver is under 2.5 m/s within ~0.1 s, well inside SHOOT_SET_T. Update the line-28 comment to say 'brake before a jumper unless a defender is within 1.0 m'. Verify with the repro scripts: normal-difficulty CPU jumpers with catch-to-press < 0.2 s should drop from ~99% to ~0% and releases above 2.5 m/s from ~90% to a minority, while A14 and A19 still pass (node test/acceptance.cjs A14 A19) and node test/unit-ai.mjs stays green.

title: DRIVE is starved by the lane test: Redrock Foxes never drive on easy/normal, one team's 2% speed edge decides all drives
evidence: 9 seeded auto games (3 seeds x 3 difficulties, test/scratch/sim-audit.cjs, ai-audit.cjs, drive-probe.cjs): handler steps in action 'drive' by team: easy 562/0, normal 442/0 (seed 7), 62/0 (21), 27/0 (99), hard 890/276. Layups+dunks per game: Foxes 0 in all six easy/normal games, Tide 1-9. Same with user team = 1 (drive-n-21-t1: 35/0). Shot-distance histogram on normal: 60 of 62 shots from 4-8 m. Lane-clear samples outside the shooting phase (normal seed 7): Tide handlers 174, Foxes 0; mean lateral offset of the on-ball guard from the handler->rim line 0.84 m vs 0.41 m. laneClear (line 490) needs no defender within DRIVE_LANE_R=1.3 m of the next 3 m of the handler->rim segment, while defence() (lines 727-728) parks the on-ball defender exactly defGap (1.3 normal, 1.7 easy) ON that segment, so the lane is blocked by construction and only opens when the guard lags; Shi Yue 0.92 vs guard Yan Zheng 0.90 and Zhou Chao 1.02 vs Hu Lie 1.00 lag enough, the mirror matchups never do.
failure: Half the roster never attacks the rim; on the default difficulty the CPU offence is 97% jump shots from 4-8 m, and which team gets drives is decided by a 0.02 rating difference rather than by beating the defender.
proposedFix: Measure lane clearance from ~1 m ahead of the handler (excluding the on-ball gap) or use a smaller lane radius (~0.8 m) plus a lateral-beat test (guard lateral offset > ~0.9 m or guard stunned/behind), and keep the DRIVE_COMMIT hysteresis so drives start when the defender is beaten rather than only when the segment is empty.
adjustedFixes: Keep SPEC's lane geometry for everyone except the assigned on-ball guard, and test the guard by whether he is beaten rather than by segment distance. In handler() (src/ai.js ~line 488-491): const guard = guardOf(p, world); const laneClear = !segmentBlocked(p.pos.x, p.pos.z, p.pos.x + G.x*len, p.pos.z + G.z*len, p.team, world, DRIVE_LANE_R, p, guard) && guardBeaten(p, guard, G); where guardBeaten returns true when guard is null, guard.state === 'stunned', dot(handler->guard, G) < 0 (guard behind the handler), or |cross(handler->guard, G)| > DRIVE_BEAT_LAT (new constant ~0.9 m, i.e. the guard is off the drive line by more than his body plus a step). segmentBlocked already has an unused skipB parameter, so no new helper is needed there. Leave DRIVE_COMMIT / DRIVE_COMMIT_NEAR hysteresis and the 0.6 + 0.05*(d-2) score untouched so a started drive still finishes. Then (a) re-run the drive probe on 3 seeds x 3 difficulties and tune DRIVE_BEAT_LAT (0.8-1.0) so drive ticks are non-zero for both teams and layup+dunk share lands in a plausible band (roughly 15-35% of CPU FGA on normal), (b) confirm A14 (each team FGM >= 1, no invariants) and the shot-distance histogram no longer collapses to 4-8 m, and (c) update SPEC 7.1's laneClear sentence to say the on-ball guard is tested by lateral offset / being behind rather than by the 1.3 m segment radius, since the current wording is what makes the lane unreachable by construction. Do not change defGap or the defence goal: the on-ball placement is correct and is what the probe/crossover is supposed to beat.

title: Difficulty does not scale CPU scoring: 69/69/75% FG against a passive human, ~50% CPU-vs-CPU at all levels
evidence: test/scratch/idle-human2.cjs (human never moves, CPU teammates defend, user possessions ended immediately, 4x120 s, seed 5): CPU FG% easy 69.1% (38/55, 1.20 pts/poss, 22 layups + 9 dunks), normal 69.4% (50/72, 1.29 pts/poss, 19 dunks), hard 75.0% (33/44, 1.10 pts/poss). Seeded CPU-vs-CPU (q=60, 4 quarters, 3 seeds): team FG% easy 58/28, 48/50, 56/62; normal 53/42, 61/29, 67/50; hard 56/48, 52/41, 73/31 - no monotonic trend. Human side (debugShoot, 120 attempts each): open 4.5 m e=0 makes 99/90/93%, e=0.08 89/84/89%, 7.3 m e=0 71/70/70% at easy/normal/hard; contested at the natural gap 4.5 m 82/48/50%. The DIFFICULTY table only changes reaction, sigma, defGap, steal, help, shootOpen, sprintProb, crossFreeze; the easy CPU's larger defGap and slower reaction give it more open drives (layups/dunks convert at 0.92-1.0), cancelling the sigma penalty.
failure: A novice who does not defend well concedes about 1.2 points per possession on easy, the same as on hard; 'easy' is easier only through the human's slightly wider green window (+0.01 vs normal), so beating the CPU requires the human to out-shoot a 69% offence.
proposedFix: Add per-difficulty CPU offence knobs: a CPU make-probability multiplier (e.g. 0.75/0.9/1.0), lower drive/sprint rates on easy, and cap the easy CPU's layup/dunk conversion (or scale base(d) for CPU layups by difficulty).

title: Block window far too generous: 67% of 6 m jumpers blocked on hard, 50% of contested layups, ~20% of all FGA in hard CPU games
evidence: test/scratch/contest-probe.cjs (human debugShoot e=0, AI on-ball defender settled at his natural gap, 60 trials each): hard d=6.0 m, defender at 0.93 m: 40/60 blocked, 12/60 made (meanP 0.41); hard d=4.5 m: 0 blocked. test/scratch/misc-probe2.cjs: normal, layup from 1.5 m with a defender 0.5 m in front: 30/60 blocked, 26 of 54 make-rolls did not score. Hard CPU-vs-CPU games: 12, 10, 10 blocks per 58/54/55 FGA (18-22%), 0 blocks in all easy/normal games (defGap 1.3/1.7 exceeds BLOCK_MAX_GAP 1.0). Mechanism: tryBlocks (lines 952-977) deflects any flight ball whose centre comes within BLOCK_R 0.40 m of the hand point during releaseAge < 0.35 s, and ai.js contest() (748-762) jumps exactly reaction s after the windup, so a defender inside 1.0 m with the arc's steep 6 m launch always intersects the sphere.
failure: On hard, a guarded mid-range jumper is blocked two times out of three and a contested layup half the time, which reads as a wall rather than a contest; NBA block rates are ~5% of FGA.
proposedFix: Shrink the block sphere/window (e.g. BLOCK_R 0.25, releaseAge < 0.15 s), require the hand to be above the ball's centre, and roll a block probability scaled by the defender's defense rating and timing instead of a deterministic geometric hit; alternatively let contest() jump with a random delay so most jumps are contests (C x 0.8), not blocks.

title: On-ball CPU defender backs away from the shooter during the windup (easy/normal)
evidence: test/scratch/contest-probe.cjs: defender teleported to 0.91 m in front of the shooter, then debugShoot e=0 (60 trials): distance at release easy 1.62 m, normal 1.30 m - 'defBackedOff' 60/60 on both; hard stays at 0.95 m only because defGap = 1.0. Resulting C at release: easy meanP 0.684 vs 0.775 for a defender already at 1.64 m (contest barely stronger up close). defence() lines 721-728 always steer the on-ball defender to D + G*gap (defGap along the delayed man->rim line) regardless of the man's state, and contest() then jumps with that backward velocity preserved (no air control), so the defender visibly hops backward while 'contesting'.
failure: Tight CPU defence is impossible: a defender who closes to 0.9 m retreats to 1.3-1.7 m while the shot goes up, so contests are always at defGap distance and the retreat-and-jump looks wrong.
proposedFix: When man.state is windup/layup/release (or the man is jumping), stop steering (mag 0) or close out toward the shooter's hand instead of returning to defGap; only resume the gap goal after the ball is released.

title: Air balls (e < -0.32) fly under the backboard and out the baseline instead of landing short
evidence: test/scratch/phys-audit.mjs, free flight with collisions, 300 shots per case: e=-0.35 from 2.5 m: rim 0%, board 0%, 87% rest out of bounds, mean rest z -16.0; from 5 m: 100% OOB, rest z -20.1; from 7.3 m: 100% OOB, rest z -24.8 (baseline is z -14.325). The target RIM - fwd*0.45 is at rim height (3.048 m) 0.45 m in front of the rim, so the ball is still ~2.9 m up when it passes under the rim and clears the board bottom (2.90 m). In-game all 12 OOB whistles across the 9 auto games were this case (ball at z -14.65, y 1.4, 2.1 s after release, kind 'three'). Airballs were 16/474 CPU shots (e < -0.32).
failure: Every air ball ends as a baseline out-of-bounds whistle ~0.3 s after passing the rim, never a short miss that bounces in front of the basket; a very early (e=-0.52) 8.2 m 'air ball' that rolls a make still swishes (p 0.052 case seen), which reads oddly with the 'early' meter flash.
proposedFix: Aim the air-ball target below the rim plane (e.g. y = RIM.y - 0.8 at 0.45-0.8 m short) or choose a lower apex so the ball drops in front of the rim, and consider forcing the roll to miss when e < AIRBALL_E.

title: Rim restitution produces very long rebounds; half of untouched misses roll out of bounds
evidence: test/scratch/phys-audit.mjs (300 misses per case, no players): late misses from 7.3 m (e=0/0.15): 100% hit the rim, 95% also the board, ball comes to rest a mean 6.6 m from the rim (rest z -6.09) with 47-50% resting beyond the sidelines/baseline; from 5 m: 52-54% OOB; from 2.5 m: 42-43% OOB. In-game hard auto game (seed 7): mean rebound catch distance 3.94 m, 36% of rebounds caught > 5 m from the rim. The 0.55 normal restitution + 0.92 tangential factor on a ~9.4 m/s arrival returns 6-8 m/s.
failure: Misses carom to the 3-point line or the sideline instead of dropping near the paint, so rebounds are chase-downs and offensive rebounds by the shooter are common.
proposedFix: Lower REST_RIM to ~0.35-0.40 and TANGENT_RIM to ~0.8 (and/or add a small random downward kick on back-rim hits) so a missed jumper stays within ~3 m of the rim.

title: Green-window misses always go long (spec 4.4 says random short/long)
evidence: chooseTarget: `else if (e < -Math.abs(g)) along = short ...; else along = RIM.r + BALL.R*(0.3+0.6*rng)` - any miss with |e| <= g falls into the long branch; there is no rng sign as the spec requires ('MISS when make rolled false but |e| <= g: treat as late with rng sign'). In the CPU game data 310/474 shots had |e| < 0.1 and their 133 misses all went to the back rim/board (rim 100%, board 95-97% in the free sim).
failure: Perfectly-timed misses are visually identical (back rim + board every time), never a front-rim roll-out.
proposedFix: For |e| <= g, pick short or long with rng.next() < 0.5 before choosing `along`.

title: Dunk: ball and hands stay below rim height, then the ball teleports into the hoop
evidence: placeOnOwner during 'dunk' sets pos.y = SHOT.RELEASE_Y + jumpY = 2.05 + 0.9*sin(...) -> max 2.95 m, rim is 3.048 m. Human dunk trace (test/scratch/misc-probe.cjs, Zhou Chao dunk 0.7): ball y 2.14 -> 2.61 -> 2.90 -> 2.92 -> 2.67 then 2.84 at RIM.x/z with state 'scored'. The humanoid hand reach (section 6: 2.05 + jump) is also < 3.05.
failure: The dunker's hands and ball never reach the rim; the ball jumps from ~2.7 m in front of the rim to rim height at t = 0.42 s, so the dunk reads as a teleport rather than a slam.
proposedFix: During the dunk raise the ball to RIM.y + 0.15 near the apex (scale the hand offset so y = lerp(2.05, RIM.y+0.15, k) with the tween), and drop it from above the rim at DUNK_BALL_T.

title: CPU never throws an interceptable pass (0 interceptions in ~900 CPU passes)
evidence: Across the 9 auto games: passes 41-49 per team per game, catches by the defence of a pass = 0, steals credited from passes = 0; steals only from dribble pokes (0-7/game). bestPassTarget skips any teammate whose lane has a defender within LANE_HARD_R + 0.1*d = 0.5-1.45 m, larger than the 0.55-0.62 m catch radius, and the human game shows the same (idle-human runs: cpu.stl 0, passOOB 0). A defender parked 0.5 m off the line does intercept (20/20 at 0.1-0.5 m, test/scratch/misc-probe2.cjs), so the mechanism works but the CPU filter makes it unreachable except by anticipation during the 0.3-0.8 s flight.
failure: Playing the passing lanes on defence never pays off against the CPU; the only turnovers a human can force are dribble steals.
proposedFix: Use the catch radius (~0.6 m) as the hard-reject radius and let the 0.8 m LANE_R only penalise the score, so a well-positioned defender occasionally picks off a pass.

title: Rematch/quit-restart keeps AI absolute-time timers, so CPU defenders stop attempting steals (and probe flips) for up to the previous game's length
evidence: Game.start() sets `w.time = 0` (game.js:222) and calls resetStats() only; it never clears `p.lastStealAt` (set to `w.time` in trySteal, game.js:922, checked as `w.time - p.lastStealAt < 1.5` at game.js:913) nor `ai.stealAt` (ai.js:733, gated by `t >= ai.stealAt` at ai.js:731; newPossession at ai.js:198 resets helpUntil/contestAt/actionT but not stealAt or probeFlipT). Headless repro test/scratch/rematch-timers2.mjs (auto=1, q=120, seed 3): game 1 first 120 s: 5 CPU steal attempts over 17 opportunity steps; after game.rematch(): max stale stealAt=744.5 s / lastStealAt=743.0 s while the whole game lasts ~820 s; game 2 first 120 s: 0 attempts over 36 opportunity steps, all 36 blocked by the stale timers. Seed 11: 4 attempts -> 1 attempt (18/19 opportunities blocked). Same for `ai.probeFlipT` (ai.js:561,563,571-573): once set, the CPU handler cannot flip its probe direction or unpin from the sideline until the new game's clock passes the old value.
failure: Tap 再来一局 (or 返回主菜单 then 开始比赛) after a normal 2:00-quarter game: for most or all of the second game the CPU on-ball defender never reaches for a steal, and CPU handlers that hit a sideline keep pushing into it instead of turning; difficulty silently drops after every rematch.
proposedFix: In Game.start() reset per-player absolute timers (`p.lastStealAt = -1e9`) and reset/reinitialise `p.ai` (or add stealAt/probeFlipT/cutAt/passReleaseAt/releaseAt to newPossession / the `ai.active` re-init path). Alternatively store these as countdowns decremented each step instead of absolute world.time stamps.

title: Halftime 'any key skips' handler also fires for the P/Esc pause, M mute and T language keys
evidence: hud.js:136 `this._on(this.doc, 'keydown', (ev) => { if (this.menu === 'halftime' && !ev.repeat && this.cb.onSkip) this.cb.onSkip(); })` runs for every key. input.js:363-365 handles KeyP/Escape (pause), KeyM (mute), KeyT (language) on the same document keydown. HUD is constructed before Input in main.js (lines 51 vs 67), so on 'P' during halftime the skip runs first (skipHalftime -> nextQuarter -> CHECK) and then togglePause pauses the freshly started quarter; 'M' mutes and skips, 'T' toggles language and skips.
failure: Desktop player presses P (or Esc) at halftime intending to pause: the halftime overlay disappears, Q3 starts and immediately shows the pause menu; pressing M or T to change a setting during halftime unexpectedly ends halftime.
proposedFix: Ignore modifier/shortcut keys in the halftime handler (skip only when Input did not consume the key, e.g. exclude KeyP/Escape/KeyM/KeyT), or route halftime skipping through Input.onPause-style callbacks so one path decides.

title: Player.reset() snaps the humanoid pose to idle twice per possession, popping defenders out of their stance at every CHECK and LIVE transition
evidence: player.js:134-136 sets `POSE.dt = 0` and calls `this.humanoid.setPose('idle', POSE)`; humanoid.js:387-392 with dt=0 assigns every joint directly (`j[k] = TGT[k]`), including hipY 0.85->0.95 and uaLZ/uaRZ ±1.2->±0.1 for the 'defend' stance. game.js enterCheck (line 387) calls reset for all six players and goLive (line 420) calls it again 1.2 s later, while Player.render (player.js:574) re-selects 'defend' for stationary defenders on the very next frame and damps back at BLEND_RATE 18.
failure: Every dead ball, the three defenders visibly jerk upright with arms dropping, then sink back into the stance over ~0.2 s, once at the whistle reset and again when play goes live.
proposedFix: Do not force a pose in reset() (let render() pick the pose and blend), or pass the real frame dt / the player's role-appropriate pose ('defend' for defenders) instead of snapping to 'idle' with dt=0.

title: README rule text does not match the implemented possession order and dead-ball timing
evidence: README.md:52-54 says possession is 'coin flip for Q1, alternating by period' and that after every dead ball 'the game resets to a check-ball formation after 1.2 s'. game.js openingPossession (lines 331-337) gives Q1=A, Q2=B, Q3=B, Q4=A (Q3 repeats Q2, per SPEC section 1), and deadBall durations are CLOCK.DEAD MADE 1.5 s / OOB 1.2 s / SHOT_CLOCK 1.2 s / TURNOVER 1.0 s (constants.js:179, game.js:433) followed by a separate 1.2 s CHECK tween (CLOCK.CHECK).
failure: A reader expecting strict alternation is surprised when the same team opens Q2 and Q3, and the '1.2 s' claim understates the ~2.2–2.7 s pause between a made basket and live play.
proposedFix: Reword to 'Q2 and Q3 go to the team that did not open Q1, Q4 to the Q1 team, OT alternates' and 'after a 1.0–1.5 s whistle the teams tween into a check-ball formation for 1.2 s before play resumes'.

title: Normal difficulty: every layup / pull-up taken near the CPU on-ball defender is blocked (74/74); a first-time player cannot score off a drive
evidence: Sim-driven 'first-timer' plays through the real Input intent (test/scratch/human-sim2.cjs, seed 5, normal): A sprint straight from the check spot, layup pressed at d<=2.0 m: 30 possessions -> 14 stripped (9 of them 0.4 s after LIVE, i.e. sprinting into the defender parked 1.47 m away), 17 layups, 17 'block' events, 0 scores. A2 same drive at run speed: 27 layups, 27 blocked, 0 scores. A4 sprint then pull-up jumper at d<=3.5 m: 30 shots, 30 blocked, 0 scores. Only A3 (release directly under the rim, d~0.45 m) scores 21/30, and spot-ups from 4.2 m score 16/30. The identical drive on EASY scores 26/30 with 0 blocks and 0 steals: the CPU contest jump fires at reaction 0.26 s (src/ai.js:748-761, src/constants.js:193) which always beats the 0.32 s layup release, and tryBlocks (src/game.js:952-975, BLOCK_R 0.40 at src/constants.js:163) is a deterministic geometric test, so the outcome is 100 % rather than a probability. Blocks are otherwise fine: a human kept 0.7 m in front blocks a CPU jumper 5-9 of 15 trials (test/scratch/block-probe2.cjs).
failure: On the default difficulty a new player who drives to the basket and presses Shoot (the most obvious 2K play) is blocked every single time and stripped half the time; the game feels rigged and the difficulty jump easy->normal is a cliff (87 % -> 0 %).
proposedFix: Make blocks probabilistic instead of geometric-deterministic in tryBlocks (e.g. roll rng < 0.35 * defender.defense once per shot when the hand test passes, and never block when the defender is already behind the shooter: dot(shooter->defender, shooter->rim) < 0), and jitter the CPU contest trigger in contest() (reaction + rng.gauss(0.08, 0.06)) so a quick layup can beat the jump; optionally lower BLOCK_R to 0.30 for layups and lengthen STEAL_CPU_INTERVAL right after CHECK so the first sprint step is not an automatic strip.

title: CPU offence is pass -> instant catch-and-shoot (0.07 s after the catch); the human defender never gets to react
evidence: test/scratch/catch-shoot.cjs (seed 5, auto game, normal): 33 of 35 CPU shots were released < 0.2 s after the receiver caught the pass (typical 0.07-0.08 s), 1.2-2.2 s after LIVE. Live sessions show the same: phoneLandscape run log, 22-p5-def-outcome.png events 'catch Hu Lie t=48.05' -> 'shot jumper t=48.12'; 15-p3-def-switch.png 'catch 17.45' -> shot; and in all three device runs the very first CPU possession is a pass at t=2.1 s and a dunk at t=3.9 s (phoneLandscape/05-p1-def-switch.png, 06-p1-def-outcome.png). Cause: a new ball handler starts with ai.actionT = -1e9 (line 454) so the SHOOT utility (line 498) is evaluated on the very next 0.1 s tick, and it always wins because off-ball defenders sag to lerp 0.35 toward the rim (OFF_LERP_ARC, line 43/738) leaving every wing receiver 'open' (>= shootOpen 1.5 m). Result: the human can only watch; switching (换人) and moving take longer than the possession.
failure: Defence possessions are decided in ~2 s before the player can switch or close out; the CPU never dribbles or probes in practice (42-43 jumpers per game, almost no drives), so defence is not interactive and every possession looks the same.
proposedFix: After a catch, hold the decision for a gather window (set ai.actionT = t and require t - ai.holdSince >= 0.4 s before 'shoot' may win, like SHOOT_SET_T), have the receiver's defender close out when a pass starts (steer to the receiver at sprint while ball.state === 'pass'), and use a smaller sag for beyond-arc shooters (OFF_LERP_ARC 0.35 -> ~0.15) so openness is not automatic; keep the instant shot only when shotClock < 3.

title: Camera hides the last ~1.5 m before the half-court line; backing up for 1 s is a silent backcourt turnover
evidence: test/scratch/misc-probe3.cjs: holding the stick 'down' from the check spot for 0.6 s -> z=-1.76 (fine), 1.0 s -> z=+0.04 -> DEAD(OOB). Screenshots test/scratch/playtest/framing-z-2.png (feet at screen y 368/390, body clipped at the knees) and framing-z-0.6.png (feet projected to y=421, off-screen; player cut at the waist, caption '失误'). LANDSCAPE lookZ=-9, z0=4.5, kz=0.20 keeps the floor beyond z~-1.5 out of frame in landscape (portrait similar). A player who backs up to set a three cannot see their own feet or the line they are about to cross.
failure: New players get 'Out of bounds' turnovers while retreating to shoot a three without any visible cue; their own player disappears off the bottom edge.
proposedFix: Pull the camera back / lower the look point when the ball is near the backcourt line, e.g. lookZ = -9 + 0.5*max(0, ballZ+4) and z0 += 0.6*max(0, ballZ+4) (damped), or clamp the human handler like the AI at z <= -0.3 with a red half-court line flash; at minimum keep the controlled player's feet on screen.

title: Play-by-play captions lag behind the action by up to two events (stale caption under a +2 banner)
evidence: test/scratch/playtest/phoneLandscape/16-p3-def-outcome.png: banner '+2' (put-back layup by 岩铮 at t=22.75) is on screen while the caption still reads '岩铮 抢下篮板' (the offensive rebound from t=21.0); the earlier '投篮不中' caption occupied the 1.8 s slot before it. caption() queues up to 6 entries and _tickCaption shows each for CAPTION_T + fade sequentially regardless of age, so captions fall 2-4 s behind during miss->rebound->score sequences.
failure: The commentary line describes the previous play while the score changes, which reads as wrong information to the player.
proposedFix: When a score/possession caption is queued, drop older queued captions (or clear the queue), and cut the currently shown caption early (e.g. after 0.6 s) when a higher-priority caption arrives; alternatively stamp captions with world.time and skip any older than 2 s.

title: Players clip through each other under the rim during dunks/rebounds
evidence: test/scratch/playtest/desktop/06-p1-def-outcome.png: the dunker and two blue defenders are rendered as one merged body under the rim (torsos and arms intersect); phoneLandscape/22-p5-def-outcome.png shows three players merged at the free-throw line. resolveSeparation keeps 0.80 m in xz but dunkers are fixed and the 0.8 m spacing plus airborne poses (arms up, jumpY) still intersect visually from the elevated camera.
failure: Bodies visibly intersect on almost every dunk and rebound scrum, which cheapens the look of the game's highlight moments.
proposedFix: Raise MOVE.SEPARATION to ~0.95 m for pairs where either player isJumping or is in 'dunk', and push non-dunkers fully away from a dunker (already 2*push) also along the dunk direction so they are not left inside the tween path; optionally shrink the blob shadow overlap by ordering shadow draw.

title: VERDICT
evidence: Played 3 offence + 3 defence possessions on phoneLandscape (seed 5, normal) with real CDP touch, 2+2 on phonePortrait, 1+1 on desktop keyboard; 50+ screenshots under test/scratch/playtest/{phoneLandscape,phonePortrait,desktop}/ with per-action state dumps in log.txt. Zero console errors, page errors or failed requests in every run; invariantsBroken stayed 0. Menu, score bug, CHECK/+2 banners, possession arrow, button relabelling (投篮/传球/变向 <-> 盖帽/换人/抢断) and the joystick ring all render correctly (01-menu.png, 03-live0.png, 06-p1-def-outcome.png). Joystick, sprint multi-touch, crossover, pass (control follows the receiver) and switch all worked on first try; the shot meter appears ~28 px right of the shooter's head with a clear green band and 完美/稍早/稍晚 flash (phoneLandscape/18-p4-three-release.png, phonePortrait/22-p4-three-release.png) and a 0.44 s hold reads as green (a jumper from 7.1 m went in: phonePortrait/23-p4-outcome.png). Court, rim, net, backboard, blob shadows and crowd look right at all three aspects; portrait layout keeps all controls reachable. The headless 15-25 fps and ~120 ms touch latency are SwiftShader artefacts, not game issues.
failure: Playable and visually solid, but not yet fun on the default difficulty: the naive drive is blocked/stripped 100 % of the time (only spot-ups and under-the-rim finishes score), and CPU possessions are 2-second pass-and-shoot sequences the defender cannot influence. Fix findings 1-3 and normal becomes a game; as shipped, recommend first-timers play on 简单/Easy.
proposedFix: Prioritise the block/contest probability and the catch-and-shoot gather window, then the backcourt camera framing; the remaining items are polish.
